tasks.title: One module for the gate's paperwork checks, with a stage set per role
tasks.summary: Factory-level. The gate's read-only pre-test checks move into one module, paperwork.ts, with a stage set per hand-off role (coder, tester, grader, gate); the gate calls it stage by stage, a preflight calls it whole, and the gate's behaviour and events are unchanged.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. Create factory/orchestrator/src/paperwork.ts as the single home of the gate's read-only pre-test checks, and make gate.ts and uiuxGate.ts call it, so a preflight (task-2's `bs results check`) and the gate can never disagree on the same input. Today these checks sit inline in gate.ts `runGateStages` (gate.ts:1185-1470, everything before the test stage), interleaved with their `emit` calls, and the private `checkGraderVerdict` (gate.ts:751-835) both validates and emits. Split each into a pure function that returns the verdict plus the exact payload the gate emits today, and keep every `emit` in gate.ts in today's order with today's payload. The paperwork stages, in the gate's order: (1) `schema`, the result record's schema check (`validateRecord`) -> `schema-invalid`; (2) `artifacts`, `checkArtifacts` -> `artifacts-missing`; (3) `commit`, `certifyCommit` -> `not-committed`; (4) `deps`, `checkWorktreeDeps` -> `deps-missing`; (5) `judges`, outstanding judge turns -> `judges-outstanding`; (6) `uiux`, when the task is ui-affecting, the checkUiux verdict -> its four reasons, in checkUiux's order: `uiux-spec-missing`, `screenshots-missing` (no tester record, or a REQUIRED_COMBOS shot missing or not on disk), `screenshots-stale`, `uiux-visual-missing`; (7) `screenshots`, the tester's own declared screenshots (tester role only, below) -> `screenshots-missing`; (8) `grader`, the grader file's shape -> `grader-invalid`. Export `checkPaperwork(input, ctx, opts)` with `input.as: 'coder' | 'tester' | 'grader' | 'gate'`, and an exported `STAGES_FOR_ROLE`. Each role checks only the stages its own hand-off can already satisfy: coder = schema, artifacts, commit, deps; tester = schema, artifacts, screenshots; grader = grader; gate = schema, artifacts, commit, deps, judges, uiux, grader, in the gate's order. For the gate role, `screenshots-missing` is the uiux stage's verdict; stage (7) is the tester's own pre-hand-back check over its declared screenshots and is not in the gate's set; both apply the same screenshot-set function, so the tester and the gate agree on the same shots. Judge turns, the uiux spec and visual turns and the tester record exist only once the wave-runner has dispatched and recorded them, so no worker role checks them. A stage outside the role's set is listed under `skipped` with why `not-checked-for-<role>`; a stage in the set whose input is absent is `skipped` with why `no-input`. The grader stage checks shape only. A well-formed grader file whose verdict is not met, or whose run_status is `dead`, is not a paperwork problem: checkPaperwork reports it as `verdicts.grader: 'fail' | 'not-graded'` and does not block on it, in every role. The gate's own `grader-fail` block is unchanged, so only the verdict, never the paperwork, blocks a task that failed its rubric. `input.alsoReported?: {role, kind}[]` names judge turns the caller is about to close (task-2's gate mode passes the closes its `gate run` line would make); the judges and uiux stages count those turns as reported. checkPaperwork itself closes nothing. Move `SCREENSHOT_RE` and `screenshotsFromArtifacts` (private today, gate.ts:451-453) into paperwork.ts and export both; gate.ts's `recordTaskResult` imports them. In uiuxGate.ts add two exports: a pure `evaluateUiux(events, input, alsoReported?)` holding today's checkUiux logic over a given event list, and a screenshot-set function (the REQUIRED_COMBOS test, uiuxGate.ts:48, plus the on-disk test through `resolveArtifactPath`). `checkUiux` keeps its declaration and becomes readLineage plus evaluateUiux. paperwork.ts's screenshots stage applies the same screenshot-set function to `screenshotsFromArtifacts` of the tester's own declared artifacts, so the tester stage and the gate's uiux stage share one combo implementation. No runtime import cycle: uiuxGate.ts does not import paperwork.ts, and paperwork.ts imports gate.ts for types only; if `checkWorktreeDeps`'s body (gate.ts:1114) moves into paperwork.ts, gate.ts keeps its export with the same declaration and delegates. Stamping the envelope stays in the CLI (results.ts `stampResultEnvelope`, as `gate run` does it today): checkPaperwork takes the complete result document. The test stage, coverage evidence, findings intake and budget check stay in gate.ts alone.
acceptance_criteria: factory/orchestrator/src/paperwork.ts exports `checkPaperwork`, `STAGES_FOR_ROLE`, `SCREENSHOT_RE`, `screenshotsFromArtifacts` and one pure function per stage; uiuxGate.ts adds only `evaluateUiux` and the screenshot-set function. gate.ts's `runGateStages` and `recordTaskResult` and uiuxGate.ts's `checkUiux` call them, and no second copy of the schema, artifact, commit, deps, judges-outstanding, screenshot-combo or grader-shape logic remains in gate.ts or uiuxGate.ts.

Gate parity, in test/paperwork.test.ts, on fixtures built by a new test/helpers/paperworkFixtures.ts: for each fixture `runGate` (with a no-op check command) returns `blocked` with reason R and `checkPaperwork({as: 'gate'})` returns `reason` R. Fixtures: unstamped envelope (a worker half with no task_id/agent/provider/model_tier/token_usage) -> `schema-invalid`; a worker shape error -> `schema-invalid`; a declared artifact never written -> `artifacts-missing`; an artifact path outside the task's artifact home -> `artifacts-missing`; uncommitted work in the worktree -> `not-committed`; a worktree whose deps check fails -> `deps-missing`; a dispatched, unreported judge turn -> `judges-outstanding`; a grader verdict outside `structured_output`, one missing criteria fields, and one with round 3 -> `grader-invalid`; a tester record whose screenshot is named without the `-<desktop|mobile>-<light|dark>.png` suffix, and one with a combo missing -> `screenshots-missing`; no uiux spec turn -> `uiux-spec-missing`; no visual turn after the tester record -> `uiux-visual-missing`. On the clean fixture both pass. The one stated difference, asserted as such: on a well-formed grader `fail` verdict and on a `dead` grader file `runGate` blocks `grader-fail`, while checkPaperwork passes with `verdicts.grader` `fail` and `not-graded`.

Role parity and stage sets: (a) coder: on the unstamped, shape-error, missing-artifact, outside-home, uncommitted and deps fixtures `checkPaperwork({as: 'coder'})` returns the reason `runGate` returns; (b) tester: on a misnamed screenshot, a missing combo, a screenshot declared but not on disk, and a clean tester result, on a session that already has the uiux spec turn, `recordTaskResult` on the tester's result followed by `checkUiux` returns R and `checkPaperwork({as: 'tester'})` on the same result document returns R (`screenshots-missing`, or a pass); (c) on a ui-affecting task with a session where no uiux spec turn, no tester record and no visual turn exist and a judge turn is dispatched and unreported, `as: 'coder'` and `as: 'tester'` on otherwise clean input pass and list judges and uiux under `skipped` with why `not-checked-for-<role>`; `as: 'grader'` skips every stage but grader.

alsoReported: on the judges-outstanding fixture and the uiux-visual-missing fixture, `checkPaperwork({as: 'gate', alsoReported})` naming the open turn passes the judges and uiux stages, and the same call without `alsoReported` blocks with the gate's reason; the events directory is unchanged either way.

Characterization: a test written first, and green on the unchanged code, drives `runGate` on the clean fixture and on the schema-invalid, artifacts-missing, not-committed, grader-invalid and screenshots-missing fixtures and pins the lineage's event types, their order and their payloads; it passes unchanged after the refactor.

Stage-order ladder: one fixture carries every paperwork defect at once. Removing the defects one at a time, `runGate` returns, in order, `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `not-committed`, `deps-missing`, `judges-outstanding`, a uiux reason, `grader-invalid`, then a pass, and `checkPaperwork({as: 'gate'})` returns the same reason at every step. `notes` shows a mutation that swaps two paperwork stages in `runGateStages` failing this test.
checkPaperwork writes nothing: a test runs it in every role on every fixture and compares the events directory and the results directory byte for byte before and after.

A stage is never reported as passed when it did not run: a stage outside the role's set is `skipped` with `not-checked-for-<role>`; a stage in the set with no input is `skipped` with `no-input` (no worktree: commit and deps; no session: judges and uiux; not ui-affecting: uiux; no grader file: grader; no tester screenshots on a task that is not ui-affecting: screenshots). A stage whose input an earlier failure left unreadable is `skipped`, not guessed.
checkPaperwork reports every problem in gate order, not only the first: a fixture with both a schema error and a missing artifact lists both, and `reason` is `schema-invalid`.
This task does not edit test/gate.test.ts, test/uiuxGate.test.ts, test/artifacts.test.ts or test/testgate.test.ts, and every assertion in them still passes.

Diff check (AC8), run by the coder before hand-back and re-run by the grader: `git diff <base>...HEAD -U0 | /usr/bin/grep -E '^\+[^+].*(\.(skip|only|todo|fails)\(|retry|quarantin|flaky|testTimeout|hookTimeout|timeout_ms|DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS|waitForLines)'`. `notes` carries its full output and, for every hit, why it is not a skip, retry, quarantine or larger timeout (a moved line whose value is unchanged, or prose that forbids the thing). tasks.title: The gate records sleep evidence on a failed test run
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Each gate check records wall-clock and monotonic time, their gap, and the load average; a failed check whose own clock gap shows the machine slept stays blocked as tests-failed and is classified execution.env-failure. Load is evidence only. Nothing is re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts, measure around each check command: wall-clock ms, monotonic ms, their gap, the 1-minute load average at start and at end, and the CPU count. Put them on each CheckResult as an optional `environment` object that `run` always sets (optional on the type so integration.ts and other constructors compile unchanged). The clock and load sources are injectable through RunOptions and GateInput, with today's real sources as the default. Export a pure classifier and one named constant, `SLEEP_GAP_MS = 30_000`. The classifier fires on the clock gap only: `clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`. Node's monotonic clock (`process.hrtime`, libuv's uv_hrtime) does not advance while the machine is suspended on the platforms the factory runs on (macOS `mach_absolute_time`, Linux `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), while the wall clock does, so the gap measures time asleep; a check cannot put the machine to sleep, so a failing suite cannot cause its own classification. 30 s is far above NTP slew and below any real suspend worth naming; the constant's comment says so and names its source. On a platform whose monotonic clock counts suspend, the gap reads about 0 and the classifier never fires, which fails safe as a plain tests-failed block. Load is recorded as evidence only and never classifies: a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself, so a load threshold would label real failures as environment failures. In gate.ts, when the test stage fails, run the classifier over each failed check's own evidence; a gap on a check that passed never classifies another check's failure. When it fires, the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned blocked GateOutcome each carry `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` and the failed check's evidence. The outcome stays `blocked`, the reason stays `tests-failed`, nothing is re-run, and the gate finalizes exactly as for any other tests-failed block. A run that passes is never classified, whatever its evidence.

tasks.objective: Repo-level fix for this repo's two named recurring test failures. Test files only; no production file changes. This also pins that SIGTERM reaches the sleep. The repeat (one report per tick, each handed out before the sleep) is already pinned in-process in test/daemon.test.ts ('hands each report to onTick before the sleep, and keeps none of them'). Confirm that it pins every per-tick behaviour the CLI test's second line pinned, and add an in-process assertion to daemon.test.ts for any it does not. The `--interval` value is the daemon's tick gap under test, not a test deadline. (b) test/providers/cli-transport.test.ts, 'times out and kills the WHOLE process group, not just the immediate child': today a real 200 ms timer can fire before the fixture has spawned its grandchild and written grandchild.pid. Keep `timeout_ms: 200` and fire it only once grandchild.pid holds a pid. The timer is the global `setTimeout` armed in src/spawn.ts:80 (`spawnCapped`), reached through `spawnOnce` (src/providers/cli-transport.ts:60-66, which arms no timer of its own); `killGroup` (src/spawn.ts:70-78) sends SIGKILL with no grace timer. Without advancing the fake clock, read and parse grandchild.pid through `setImmediate` polling (not faked) until it holds a positive integer pid; a missing or still-empty file means keep polling, never advance (read and parse, never mere existence). The poll races the pending `runCliJudge` promise: attach a settle handler to that promise when the call is made, and if it settles (resolves or rejects) before a parseable pid appears, because the fake-judge child died or exited early, the test fails at once with an assertion that says so (for example 'runCliJudge settled before grandchild.pid held a pid') instead of polling until the test timeout. No extra deadline is needed and none is added: vitest arms each test's timeout with the timers it saved before any fakes were installed, so `vi.useFakeTimers` cannot freeze it and the poll cannot hang past the unchanged test timeout. Then `vi.advanceTimersByTime(200)`, await the `provider.timeout` rejection, and restore real timers in a `finally` before the liveness wait, which checks the parsed pid. Add an optional start delay to the fixture's `slow-grandchild` mode (default 0, every other mode unchanged) and a second case that delays the grandchild by more than `timeout_ms` and still passes. Under fake time the fixture's real start delay cannot make the 200 ms timer fire early, which is what makes the delayed case meaningful: with real timers that case kills the group before the grandchild exists. No production seam is added.

Split each into a pure function that returns the verdict plus the exact payload the gate emits today, and keep every `emit` in gate.ts in today's order with today's payload. The paperwork stages, in the gate's order: (1) `schema`, the result record's schema check (`validateRecord`) -> `schema-invalid`; (2) `artifacts`, `checkArtifacts` -> `artifacts-missing`; (3) `commit`, `certifyCommit` -> `not-committed`; (4) `deps`, `checkWorktreeDeps` -> `deps-missing`; (5) `judges`, outstanding judge turns -> `judges-outstanding`; (6) `uiux`, when the task is ui-affecting, the checkUiux verdict -> its four reasons, in checkUiux's order: `uiux-spec-missing`, `screenshots-missing` (no tester record, or a REQUIRED_COMBOS shot missing or not on disk), `screenshots-stale`, `uiux-visual-missing`; (7) `screenshots`, the tester's own declared screenshots (tester role only, below) -> `screenshots-missing`; (8) `grader`, the grader file's shape -> `grader-invalid`. Export `checkPaperwork(input, ctx, opts)` with `input.as: 'coder' | 'tester' | 'grader' | 'gate'`, and an exported `STAGES_FOR_ROLE`. Each role checks only the stages its own hand-off can already satisfy: coder = schema, artifacts, commit, deps; tester = schema, artifacts, screenshots; grader = grader; gate = schema, artifacts, commit, deps, judges, uiux, grader, in the gate's order. For the gate role, `screenshots-missing` is the uiux stage's verdict; stage (7) is the tester's own pre-hand-back check over its declared screenshots and is not in the gate's set; both apply the same screenshot-set function, so the tester and the gate agree on the same shots. Judge turns, the uiux spec and visual turns and the tester record exist only once the wave-runner has dispatched and recorded them, so no worker role checks them. A stage outside the role's set is listed under `skipped` with why `not-checked-for-<role>`; a stage in the set whose input is absent is `skipped` with why `no-input`. The grader stage checks shape only. A well-formed grader file whose verdict is not met, or whose run_status is `dead`, is not a paperwork problem: checkPaperwork reports it as `verdicts.grader: 'fail' | 'not-graded'` and does not block on it, in every role. The gate's own `grader-fail` block is unchanged, so only the verdict, never the paperwork, blocks a task that failed its rubric. `input.alsoReported?: {role, kind}[]` names judge turns the caller is about to close (task-2's gate mode passes the closes its `gate run` line would make); the judges and uiux stages count those turns as reported. checkPaperwork itself closes nothing. Move `SCREENSHOT_RE` and `screenshotsFromArtifacts` (private today, gate.ts:451-453) into paperwork.ts and export both; gate.ts's `recordTaskResult` imports them. In uiuxGate.ts add two exports: a pure `evaluateUiux(events, input, alsoReported?)` holding today's checkUiux logic over a given event list, and a screenshot-set function (the REQUIRED_COMBOS test, uiuxGate.ts:48, plus the on-disk test through `resolveArtifactPath`). `checkUiux` keeps its declaration and becomes readLineage plus evaluateUiux. paperwork.ts's screenshots stage applies the same screenshot-set function to `screenshotsFromArtifacts` of the tester's own declared artifacts, so the tester stage and the gate's uiux stage share one combo implementation. Stamping the envelope stays in the CLI (results.ts `stampResultEnvelope`, as `gate run` does it today): checkPaperwork takes the complete result document. The test stage, coverage evidence, findings intake and budget check stay in gate.ts alone.

tasks.title: The gate records sleep evidence on a failed test run
tasks.summary: Factory-level. Each gate check records wall-clock and monotonic time over its own process, their gap, and the load average; a failed check whose own clock gap shows the machine slept stays blocked as tests-failed and is classified execution.env-failure. The heavy-lock wait is outside the window, a lock-wait timeout never classifies, load is evidence only, and nothing is re-run.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix. In factory/orchestrator/src/testgate.ts, measure each check command: wall-clock ms, monotonic ms, their gap, the 1-minute load average at start and at end, and the CPU count. Put them beside the check results, never inside CheckResult (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-8de89739): test/testgate.test.ts:87-89 pins a passing check's CheckResult with an exact `toEqual`, and AC3 keeps that assertion unchanged. RunResult gains an optional `environment` array that `run` always sets: one entry per entry of `results`, in the same order, each `{name, window: 'command' | 'none', wall_ms, monotonic_ms, clock_gap_ms, load_1m_start, load_1m_end, cpus}`. It is index-aligned and carries the check's name rather than being keyed by name, because nothing makes check names in a checks file unique (cli.ts `readChecksFile`). CheckResult's declaration does not change, so integration.ts, which maps `results` into its own list, and every other CheckResult constructor and assertion are untouched; `runCumulative` returns `run`'s RunResult and so carries the array too. The gate's `testgate-result` payload carries the array as `environment`, beside `pass` and `results` (gate.ts `runGate`, the `emit('testgate-result', ...)` call at gate.ts:1459-1465); event.schema.json leaves a payload's shape open, so no schema changes. Where the window sits (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-b1e1257b): it brackets the check's own process and nothing else. It opens immediately before `runOne` spawns the command and closes when that process closes, so the evidence measures the check, not the queue. For a heavy check (`isHeavyCheck`, testgate.ts:39-47, run through `runHeavy`, testgate.ts:326-360 at 99e7fe64) that is inside the `withHeavyLock` callback, after the lease is held: the lock wait stays in `lock_wait_ms`, measured as today, and never enters `clock_gap_ms`. A check whose lock wait timed out (`runHeavy`'s catch, `reason: 'heavy.wait-timeout'`) spawned no command, so its `environment` entry has `window: 'none'`, zero `wall_ms`, `monotonic_ms` and `clock_gap_ms`, one load sample taken when the wait ended as both `load_1m_start` and `load_1m_end`, and `cpus`; it never classifies, and its block stays `tests-failed` with its own `reason: heavy.wait-timeout` and no `error_class`. Every other entry has `window: 'command'`. The clock and load sources are injectable through RunOptions and GateInput, with today's real sources as the default; GateInput gains no lock option. Export a pure classifier and one named constant, `SLEEP_GAP_MS = 30_000`. The classifier fires on a `window: 'command'` entry whose clock gap is at least the constant: `clock_gap_ms >= SLEEP_GAP_MS`. Node's monotonic clock (`process.hrtime`, libuv's uv_hrtime) does not advance while the machine is suspended on the platforms the factory runs on (macOS `mach_absolute_time`, Linux `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), while the wall clock does, so the gap measures time asleep; a check cannot put the machine to sleep, so a failing suite cannot cause its own classification. 30 s is far above NTP slew and below any real suspend worth naming; the constant's comment says so and names its source. On a platform whose monotonic clock counts suspend, the gap reads about 0 and the classifier never fires, which fails safe as a plain tests-failed block. Load is recorded as evidence only and never classifies: a full suite raises the 1-minute load average itself, so a load threshold would label real failures as environment failures. In gate.ts, when the test stage fails, run the classifier over each failed check's own `environment` entry; a gap on a check that passed never classifies another check's failure. When it fires, the `testgate-result` payload, the `gate-outcome` payload and the returned blocked GateOutcome each carry `error_class: 'execution.env-failure'` and the failed check's evidence. The outcome stays `blocked`, the reason stays `tests-failed`, nothing is re-run, and the gate finalizes exactly as for any other tests-failed block. A run that passes is never classified, whatever its evidence. Tests never take the machine's heavy lock: test/setup.ts already points BS_HEAVY_LOCK_DIR at a per-file temp directory (setup.ts:40-48); on top of that, test/gateEnvEvidence.test.ts marks its checks `heavy: false` (or gives them non-heavy names), and a test/testgate.test.ts case about a heavy check passes `heavyLock: {lockDir}` with a `mkdtemp` directory, as test/heavyLock.test.ts does. (b) test/providers/cli-transport.test.ts, 'times out and kills the WHOLE process group, not just the immediate child': today a real 200 ms timer can fire before the fixture has spawned its grandchild and written grandchild.pid. tasks.summary: Factory-level. Lesson recurrence counts a blocked gate-outcome under the taxonomy class its reason maps to, or under the error_class the gate stamped on a slept run; an unmapped reason counts nowhere and a task counts once per class. Read at recurrence time, so the gate.ts hub is untouched.
tasks.objective: Factory-level fix for finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-a8609c17 (operator answer 1a, bs-gate-bounce-run-2026-10-29#2). Line numbers are at main 99e7fe64. Make a blocked gate-outcome count, decided at recurrence time, so nothing touches the gate.ts hub. (1) In lessonRecurrence.ts export `GATE_BLOCK_ERROR_CLASSES`, typed `Readonly<Record<GateBlockedReason, string | null>>` over the reason union errorIssues.ts exports (imported type-only; test/errorIssues.test.ts already ties that union to gate.ts's GateOutcome at compile time), so a new gate reason fails to compile until it is mapped. The map, decided in this plan: `schema-invalid`, `artifacts-missing`, `screenshots-missing` and `grader-invalid` -> `contract.schema-violation` (the Result against result.schema.json, its declared artifacts and screenshots, the grader file against grader-verdict.schema.json; the approved lessons in factory/policies/lessons.md about the artifact check and about where a judge's verdict sits already carry this class; cite the class, never a lesson id, in code and notes (finding f-bs-gate-bounce/integration-07457ae1)); `not-committed` -> `contract.uncommitted-work` (taxonomy.yml defines that class as this check); `deps-missing` -> `execution.env-failure` (the worktree lacks the toolchain its checks need); `tests-failed` -> `execution.test-failure`; and null, counting toward no class, for `judges-outstanding`, `uiux-spec-missing`, `uiux-visual-missing` and `screenshots-stale` (the wave-runner's own sequencing, not a failure of the work), `grader-fail` (a rubric verdict; the criteria it failed can be of any class), `coverage-evidence` (a reporter or include-glob gap, wave.md step 7) and `findings` (each finding carries its own category). (2) One exported rule, used by both files and restated by neither, decides which events count and under what class: an `error-logged` event counts under `payload.error`, as today; a `gate-outcome` whose `payload.outcome` is `blocked` counts under `payload.error_class` when that is a non-empty string (task-3's `execution.env-failure` on a slept run wins over the reason's class), else under `GATE_BLOCK_ERROR_CLASSES[payload.reason]`; a reason the map does not hold, or maps to null, counts nowhere, and so does every other event. The task and the epic are read as today (`taskOf`: the envelope `task_id`, else `payload.task_ref`; the epic: `payload.epic_id`, else the task id's epic), and `errorClassCounts` still counts distinct tasks per class, so a task that is both blocked and logged under one class, or blocked twice, counts once.
